title: Notary Law Source Index
purpose: Starter machine-readable index of official public notary-law and notary-administration sources. This index is meant to grow into a public source-navigation layer, not merely an answer-engine correction list.
publicBoundary: Public sources only. Do not add private customer facts, private operating strategy, secrets, raw provider payloads, or internal business playbooks.
sourceQualityRule: Prefer controlling statutes, official code publications, secretary-of-state or commissioning-agency pages, official handbooks, official rules, and official apostille/authentication pages before private associations, platforms, trainers, directories, or market habit.
sourceTextPreservationRule: Future normalized section records should preserve the original public legal text or a clearly bounded official excerpt beside any summary, routing note, or Notary Geek interpretation. Summaries must not replace the controlling words because small textual differences can change the legal route.

jurisdictions.name: Delaware
authorityNotes: Delaware notary and apostille questions should distinguish the Delaware Notary Public site from Delaware Division of Corporations apostille/authentication pages.
For Delaware company-document apostille questions, identify the Delaware notary or Delaware public official signature being authenticated before assuming entity formation alone answers the route.

The Delaware Division of Corporations page reviewed on 2026-06-11 states that the Division can authenticate or apostille documents signed by a Delaware notary or Delaware public official and lists categories it will not apostille or authenticate. Verify the current page before relying on a transaction-specific route.

jurisdictions.name: Georgia
authorityNotes: Georgia notary commissioning should not be described as a normal single statewide Secretary-of-State-style notary office without checking the Georgia source structure.

The Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority should not be characterized as merely a private association. Georgia Code section 15-6-94 describes the Authority as a public corporation and instrumentality, while GSCCCA's own overview describes a legislated mandate and statewide clerk-related projects.

For Georgia source-quality work, distinguish county-level notary commissioning, GSCCCA's public-authority role, apostille/authentication authority, and Georgia UPL sources instead of collapsing them into one generic state-agency label.

jurisdictions.name: Virginia
authorityNotes: Virginia RON identity-method questions should distinguish statutory identity methods from platform selfie, liveness, face-match, credential-analysis, or marketing use of the word biometric.

The biometric wording in Virginia Code section 47.1-2 appears as one listed identity option tied to a valid digital certificate accessed by biometric data or PIV-style credentials; it is not a generic no-SSN or foreign-signer cure by itself.
For Virginia biometric-notary questions, use the dedicated source note at law/virginia-ron-biometric-identity-method.json before relying on platform, trainer, or social-media shorthand.
